title: Power Automate process mining: custom KPIs in the process intelligence experience
summary: The roadmap facts, licensing background and ownership controls are supported. The ownership API is valid, including its JSON header and owner binding; the only correction is to put the deciding property in the control note and shorten the displayed call to its method and path.

claims.claim: Process ownership can be reassigned in Power Platform admin center through environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Reassign records.
claims.quote: Select the environment where the process is located. ... On the command bar, select Settings. ... Under Users + permissions, select Users. ... Select the leaving user. ... On the command bar, select Reassign records.

claims.claim: PATCH to the versioned msdyn_pminferredtasks record endpoint with Content-Type application/json and ownerid@odata.bind set to a systemusers record changes its owner.
claims.quote: Assign ... PATCH /msdyn_pminferredtasks(msdyn_pminferredtaskid) Update the ownerid property.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api.call to 'PATCH <organization-uri>/api/data/v9.2/msdyn_pminferredtasks(<msdyn_pminferredtaskid>)'. Add to controls[0].note: 'The request body sets ownerid through ownerid@odata.bind to systemusers(<new-owner-systemuserid>).'. The existing endpoint and property are valid; the cited Web API entity reference documents the v9.2 path, PATCH support and ownerid navigation property. The already-cited update and association guides support Content-Type: application/json and @odata.bind, so the pre-check's missing-header match is not an API error.

claims.claim: The new owner needs appropriate privileges on the entities associated with the transferred records.
claims.quote: Reassignment requirement: The target user should have the appropriate privileges on the different entities associated with the transferred records.
